plain: In the 1960s, a physicist named James McDonald is said to have confronted J. Allen Hynek, a scientist who had explained away UFO sightings in Michigan as swamp gas. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source. He calls McDonald "a serious physicist" and has him tell Hynek that he had been taking part in a cover-up and that "what you saw in Michigan wasn't swamp gas." An online researcher who goes by RedPandaKoala tells it as the turning point for Hynek. He says McDonald came to him "super pissed" and told him "what you're doing to science is horrible," and that this was a big part of why Hynek later changed his stance and came clean. It matters because it would show an official debunker being pushed into taking UFOs seriously.
